# CUDA 11.4 device functions by architecture

The ollama37 image builds native code for sm_37, 50, 52, 60, 61, 70, 75, 80 and 86 with CUDA 11.4. This file lists what CUDA 11.4 lets device code use on each of those targets.

**Sources**
- **C++ functions:** read from the `__CUDA_ARCH__` guards in the CUDA 11.4 headers (`cuda_cudart` 11.4.148 and `cuda_nvcc` 11.4.152 redistributables).
- **PTX instructions:** assembled with the CUDA 11.4 `ptxas` (build `cuda_11.4.r11.4/compiler.30521435_0`) for each target. ✓ means it assembled; ✗ means `ptxas` rejected it.

## Targets

| Arch | Generation | Example cards |
|---|---|---|
| sm_37 | Kepler | Tesla K80 |
| sm_50, sm_52 | Maxwell | GTX 750, GTX 9xx, Tesla M40 |
| sm_60 | Pascal (GP100) | Tesla P100 |
| sm_61 | Pascal | GTX 10xx, Tesla P40 |
| sm_70 | Volta | Tesla V100, Titan V |
| sm_75 | Turing | RTX 20xx, GTX 16xx, Tesla T4 |
| sm_80 | Ampere (GA100) | A100 |
| sm_86 | Ampere | RTX 30xx, A40 |

## Feature matrix

| Feature | Function or instruction | 37 | 50/52 | 60 | 61 | 70 | 75 | 80/86 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Warp shuffle and vote | `__shfl_*_sync`, `__ballot_sync`, `__syncwarp` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Read-only and cache-hinted loads | `__ldg`, `__ldcg`, `__stcs` … | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 64-bit integer atomics | `atomicMin/Max/And/Or/Xor` on long long | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Half conversion (storage only) | `__float2half`, `__half2float` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Half arithmetic | `__hadd2`, `__hfma2`, `__hmul2` (PTX `fma.rn.f16x2`) | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Double atomicAdd, scoped atomics | `atomicAdd(double*)`, `atomic*_block`, `atomic*_system` | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `half2` atomicAdd | `atomicAdd(__half2*)` | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| 8-bit dot product | `__dp4a`, `__dp2a_lo/hi` (PTX `dp4a`) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `half` atomicAdd | `atomicAdd(__half*)` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Warp match, nanosleep | `__match_any_sync`, `__nanosleep` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| WMMA fp16 tensor core | `nvcuda::wmma` half, m16n16k16 | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| MMA m8n8k4 f16 | PTX `mma.sync…m8n8k4` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| MMA m16n8k8 f16 | PTX `mma.sync…m16n8k8` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| MMA m8n8k16 int8 | PTX `mma.sync…m8n8k16.s8` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Matrix load from shared memory | PTX `ldmatrix` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ |
| MMA m16n8k16 f16, m16n8k32 int8 | PTX `mma.sync…m16n8k16`, `…m16n8k32` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| bf16 arithmetic, bf16 MMA | `__hfma2(__nv_bfloat162)`, PTX `.bf16` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Hardware async copy | `__pipeline_memcpy_async`², PTX `cp.async` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Half max/min, fused ReLU | `__hmax2`, `__hmin2`, `__hfma2_relu` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Warp reduce | `__reduce_add_sync` … (PTX `redux.sync`) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
| Matrix transpose in registers | PTX `movmatrix` | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

¹ **Half arithmetic on sm_61 compiles, but the hardware runs it at 1/64 of the FP32 rate.** This is a property of the chip, not of CUDA 11.4. It is why ggml-cuda excludes cc 610 from "fast FP16".

² **`__pipeline_memcpy_async` exists from sm_70, but only sm_80 and up use the hardware copy.** On sm_70 and sm_75 the header falls back to an ordinary load and store (`cuda_pipeline_helpers.h:68-72`).

**`movmatrix` fails on every target.** It needs PTX ISA 7.8, which arrived in CUDA 11.8. CUDA 11.4's `ptxas` stops at PTX 7.4: `Unsupported .version 7.8; current version is '7.4'`.

## C++ functions per minimum architecture

This counts the functions each header declares under each `__CUDA_ARCH__` threshold. Thresholds without a column in the matrix (sm_20, 30, 32, 35, 53) are all at or below a target we build, except sm_53, which is at or below sm_60.

| Min arch | Header | Count | Functions |
|---|---|--:|---|
| any | `device_atomic_functions.h` | 37 | 32-bit `atomicAdd/Sub/Exch/Min/Max/Inc/Dec/CAS/And/Or/Xor` |
| any | `cuda_fp16.hpp` | 82 | half and half2 types, conversions (`__float2half*`, `__half2float`, `__half2int_*` …) |
| any | `cuda_bf16.hpp` | 20 | bf16 types and float↔bf16 conversion only |
| sm_20 | `sm_20_intrinsics.h` | 82 | `__syncthreads_count/and/or`, `__threadfence_system`, directed-rounding double math, `__cvta_*`, `__isShared/Global` |
| sm_30 | `sm_30_intrinsics.h` | 13 | `__shfl_*_sync`, `__all_sync`, `__any_sync`, `__ballot_sync`, `__activemask`, `__syncwarp`, `__fns` |
| sm_32 | `sm_32_intrinsics.h` | 14 | `__ldg`, `__ldca/cg/cs/cv/lu`, `__stcg/cs/wb/wt`, `__funnelshift_*` |
| sm_32 | `sm_32_atomic_functions.h` | 15 | 64-bit `atomicMin/Max/And/Or/Xor` |
| sm_53 | `cuda_fp16.hpp` | 65 | `__hadd(2)`, `__hsub(2)`, `__hmul(2)`, `__hfma(2)`, `__hdiv`, `__hneg`, `__habs`, compares (`__heq2`, `__hlt2` …), `h2sin/h2cos/h2exp` … |
| sm_60 | `sm_60_atomic_functions.h` | 24 | `atomicAdd(double)`, `atomic*_block`, `atomic*_system` |
| sm_60 | `cuda_fp16.hpp` | 1 | `atomicAdd(__half2*)` |
| sm_61 | `sm_61_intrinsics.h` | 3 | `__dp4a`, `__dp2a_lo`, `__dp2a_hi` |
| sm_70 | `sm_70_rt.h` | 4 | `__match_all_sync`, `__match_any_sync`, `__nanosleep`, 16-bit `atomicCAS` |
| sm_70 | `cuda_fp16.hpp` | 1 | `atomicAdd(__half*)` |
| sm_70 | `mma.h` | — | `nvcuda::wmma` fragments, `load/store_matrix_sync`, `mma_sync` for half/float |
| sm_72 | `mma.h` | — | wmma with `signed/unsigned char` (int8). No target we build is sm_72, so this first applies at sm_75. |
| sm_73 | `mma.h` | — | `experimental::precision::u4/s4/b1` (sub-byte wmma). This first applies at sm_75. |
| sm_80 | `mma.h` | — | wmma with `__nv_bfloat16`, `precision::tf32`, `double` (m8n8k4) |
| sm_80 | `cuda_bf16.hpp` | 153 | all bf16 arithmetic, compares and conversions to int |
| sm_80 | `cuda_fp16.hpp` | 10 | `__hmax(2)`, `__hmin(2)`, `*_nan` variants, `__hfma(2)_relu` |
| sm_80 | `sm_80_rt.h` | 10 | `__reduce_{add,min,max,and,or,xor}_sync`, `__nv_memcpy_async_shared_global_{4,8,16}`, `__nv_associate_access_property` |

I deleted the three study files and wrote a new list in their place: `cuda-11.4-functions-by-arch.md` in the repo root. It was built from the real CUDA 11.4 toolchain, not from memory or reasoning:
- **C++ functions:** I downloaded NVIDIA's CUDA 11.4 headers and grouped every device function by the minimum architecture its `__CUDA_ARCH__` guard requires.
- **Tensor-core and async-copy instructions:** these are inline assembly (PTX), not header functions. I assembled test snippets with the CUDA 11.4 PTX assembler for each target and recorded which ones it accepted.

Where each generation stops under CUDA 11.4:

| Arch | Adds |
|---|---|
| sm_37 K80, sm_50/52 Maxwell | Warp shuffle, cached loads and 64-bit atomics. No half-precision arithmetic, no 8-bit dot product, no tensor cores. |
| sm_60 P100 | Half arithmetic, double `atomicAdd`, scoped atomics |
| sm_61 GTX 10xx, P40 | `__dp4a` (8-bit dot product). Half arithmetic compiles, but the chip runs it at 1/64 speed. |
| sm_70 V100 | WMMA fp16 tensor cores, MMA m8n8k4, `__match_any_sync` |
| sm_75 Turing | MMA m16n8k8, int8 MMA, `ldmatrix` |
| sm_80/86 Ampere | MMA m16n8k16, bf16, hardware async copy (`cp.async`), `__reduce_*_sync`, half max/min |

The file is untracked and nothing else changed. If it's useful, I could next add a column showing which of these functions ggml-cuda actually calls.

# Where ollama37 and upstream use the CUDA 11.4 functions

This file takes each row of [cuda-11.4-functions-by-arch.md](cuda-11.4-functions-by-arch.md) and records where two code trees use it, and under which guard. The scope is sm_37 to sm_86 (Kepler to RTX 30); HIP, MUSA and Hopper/Blackwell branches are left out.

| Tree | Source |
|---|---|
| **ollama37** | `ml/backend/ggml/ggml/src/ggml-cuda`, ggml `7049736b` (`Makefile.sync`) |
| **upstream** | Ollama v0.33.3 has no ggml-cuda of its own. Its GPU code is llama.cpp `b10729` (`LLAMA_CPP_VERSION`), path `ggml/src/ggml-cuda` |

Both trees select code with the same arch macros:

| Macro | ollama37 | upstream | Defined on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FP16_AVAILABLE` | `common.cuh:250` | `common.cuh:257` | cc ≥ 600 |
| `FAST_FP16_AVAILABLE` | `common.cuh:254` | `common.cuh:261` | cc ≥ 600 **and** cc ≠ 610 |
| `VOLTA_MMA_AVAILABLE` | — | `common.cuh:274` | cc == 700 |
| `TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE` | `common.cuh:262` | `common.cuh:278` | cc ≥ 750 |
| `AMPERE_MMA_AVAILABLE`, `CP_ASYNC_AVAILABLE` | `common.cuh:266,270` | `common.cuh:282,290` | cc ≥ 800 |
| `GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A` | `common.cuh:81` | `common.cuh:51` | 610 |

## Function use by tree

"Fallback" means the code has a replacement path for archs below the guard. "Off" means the kernel compiles to `NO_DEVICE_CODE` there and the host must not select it.

| Function (min arch) | ollama37 | upstream | Below the guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| `__shfl_*_sync` (any) | 29 uses in 9 files. 20 unguarded, used by every kernel's warp reductions. | 42 uses, 36 unguarded | — (works on sm_37) |
| `__ballot_sync`, `__syncwarp` (any) | 2, `common.cuh` | 2, `common.cuh` | — |
| `__ldg` (sm_32) | 1, `pool2d.cu:39`, `#if __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 350` | 2, `pool1d.cu`, `pool2d.cu` | — |
| 32-bit `atomicAdd` (any) | 1, `count-equal.cu:25` | same | — |
| 64-bit and other atomics | unused | unused | — |
| Half conversion (any) | 83 uses, 50 unguarded | 93 uses, 58 unguarded | — (works on sm_37) |
| Half arithmetic `__hadd2`/`__hfma2`… (sm_53) | 12 uses, all under `FP16_AVAILABLE`, `FAST_FP16_AVAILABLE` or `== VOLTA` | 7 uses, same guards | Fallback: FP32 math on sm_37/50/52. sm_61 compiles it but is excluded from `FAST_FP16`. |
| `__dp4a` (sm_61) | via `ggml_cuda_dp4a`, `common.cuh:561`, `#if __CUDA_ARCH__ >= GGML_CUDA_CC_DP4A` | same, `common.cuh:734` | Fallback: 4 scalar byte multiplies on sm_37/50/52/60 |
| `__match_any_sync`, `__nanosleep` (sm_70) | unused | 1, `allreduce.cu:165` (multi-GPU all-reduce, `>= VOLTA`) | — |
| WMMA fp16 (sm_70) | Flash-attention WMMA kernel, `fattn-wmma-f16.cu:66`, only on `__CUDA_ARCH__ == VOLTA` | FA WMMA kernel removed. WMMA only in `lightning-indexer.cu:114` under `TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE` | Off |
| PTX `mma.sync m8n8k4` (sm_70) | unused | `mma.cuh:1372`, `VOLTA_MMA_AVAILABLE` (Volta now uses the MMA path) | Off |
| PTX `mma.sync m16n8k8`, int8 `m8n8k16` (sm_75) | `mma.cuh`, 18 uses under `TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE` and `< AMPERE` | same 18 | Off |
| PTX `ldmatrix` (sm_75) | `mma.cuh:243-300` (`load_ldmatrix*`), every one under `TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE`. Called from `mmq.cuh`, `mmf.cuh`, `fattn-mma-f16.cuh`. | same pattern | Off |
| PTX `mma.sync m16n8k16`, `m16n8k32` (sm_80) | `mma.cuh`, 8 uses under `>= AMPERE` | same 8 | Turing uses two `m16n8k8` instead |
| bf16 MMA (sm_80) | `mma.cuh:455`, `AMPERE_MMA_AVAILABLE` | `mma.cuh:1187` | Off |
| bf16 type and conversion (any) | 41 unguarded uses: storage and float↔bf16 conversion only | 65 | — |
| `cp.async` (sm_80) | `cp-async.cuh:22`, `CP_ASYNC_AVAILABLE` | same | Fallback: ordinary loads |
| `__hmax`/`__hmax2` (sm_80) | `common.cuh:482,498`, used only when `CUDART_VERSION >= 11070` | same, `common.cuh:655,671` | CUDA 11.4 always takes the `fmaxf` fallback |
| `__reduce_add_sync` (sm_80) | `common.cuh:400`, `>= AMPERE` | `common.cuh:445` | Fallback: shuffle reduction |
| PTX `movmatrix` (PTX 7.8) | `mma.cuh:22`, only when `CUDART_VERSION >= 11080` | `mma.cuh:26`, same | CUDA 11.4 compiles a `__shfl_sync` replacement (`mma.cuh:39`). ollama37 adds `ggml_cuda_should_use_mma_fattn` (`fattn-mma-f16.cuh:11`), which disables the MMA flash-attention kernel below 11.8; its comment says the replacement gives wrong results. |

## CUDA-version switches that CUDA 11.4 trips

These `CUDART_VERSION` checks pick a different path because the toolkit is 11.4, whatever the GPU.

| Check | ollama37 | upstream | Effect on an 11.4 build |
|---|---|---|---|
| `>= 11040` | `cp-async.cuh:25` | same | L2-prefetch `cp.async` variants on. Only reached on sm_80+. |
| `>= 11070` | `common.cuh:129` (`GGML_CUDA_USE_CUB`), `ssm-scan.cu:1` | `common.cuh:110`, `ssm-scan.cu:1` | No CUB: the hand-written scan and sort paths are used |
| `>= 11070` (`CUDART_HMAX`) | `common.cuh:482,498` | `common.cuh:655,671` | Half max goes through float |
| `>= 11080` | `mma.cuh:22` | `mma.cuh:26` | No `movmatrix` (see above) |
| `>= 11080` | — | `vendors/cuda.h:13` (`FP8_AVAILABLE`), `common.cuh:119` (`GGML_CUDA_USE_PDL`) | Upstream loses FP8 and programmatic dependent launch. PDL only acts on Hopper anyway. |
| `>= 12000` | `common.cuh:191`, `ggml-cuda.cu:3139` | `common.cuh:194`, `ggml-cuda.cu:2634` | cuBLAS error strings and the old `cudaGraphExecUpdate` signature |
| `>= 12000` (`CUDART_HMASK`) | `common.cuh:522` | — | Half2 mask compare emulated through float |
| `>= 12080` | `common.cuh:640` | `common.cuh:823`, `quantize.cu:12,239,…` | e8m0 (MXFP4 scale) conversion in software. Upstream also gates its FP4 quantize paths here. |

## Findings

- **Code that runs on sm_37 uses only the unguarded rows:** shuffles, votes, `__ldg`, 32-bit `atomicAdd`, and half/bf16 as storage with conversion. Every newer function has a fallback or sits behind an arch guard. This matches the ptxas results: an arch that lacks an instruction never compiles it.
- **The K80 pays for two fallbacks on hot paths:** `ggml_cuda_dp4a` becomes four scalar multiplies (quantized matmul, every Q4/Q8 model), and half arithmetic runs as FP32.
- **Upstream `b10729` adds nothing new for sm_37 to sm_86 from the table.** Its only new uses are `__nanosleep` in multi-GPU all-reduce and WMMA in the lightning indexer. It replaced Volta's WMMA flash-attention kernel with `mma m8n8k4` under a new `VOLTA_MMA_AVAILABLE`.
- **On sm_37 to sm_86, CUDA 11.4 itself costs `movmatrix`, CUB and native half max.** Upstream's other version-gated features (FP8, FP4, PDL) target Hopper and Blackwell.

| `>= 12080` | `common.cuh:640` | `common.cuh:823`, `quantize.cu:12,239,…` | e8m0 (MXFP4 scale) conversion in software. Upstream also gates its FP4 quantize paths here. |

## Findings

- **Code that runs on sm_37 uses only the unguarded rows:** shuffles, votes, `__ldg`, 32-bit `atomicAdd`, and half/bf16 as storage with conversion. Every newer function has a fallback or sits behind an arch guard. This matches the ptxas results: an arch that lacks an instruction never compiles it.
- **The K80 pays for two fallbacks on hot paths:** `ggml_cuda_dp4a` becomes four scalar multiplies (quantized matmul, every Q4/Q8 model), and half arithmetic runs as FP32.
- **Upstream `b10729` adds nothing new for sm_37 to sm_86 from the table.** Its only new uses are `__nanosleep` in multi-GPU all-reduce and WMMA in the lightning indexer. It replaced Volta's WMMA flash-attention kernel with `mma m8n8k4` under a new `VOLTA_MMA_AVAILABLE`.
- **On sm_37 to sm_86, CUDA 11.4 itself costs `movmatrix`, CUB and native half max.** Upstream's other version-gated features (FP8, FP4, PDL) target Hopper and Blackwell.

content.text:
I searched ollama37 and upstream Ollama for every function in the table and wrote the results to `cuda-11.4-usage.md` in the repo root. Upstream Ollama v0.33.3 no longer has CUDA code of its own. Its GPU code is llama.cpp `b10729`, so that is the tree I searched as "ollama and llama.cpp". ollama37 uses its vendored ggml `7049736b`.

- **A K80 only ever runs the basic functions.** Warp shuffles and votes, `__ldg`, 32-bit `atomicAdd`, and half/bf16 as storage with conversion have no arch guard. Every newer function either has a fallback or is compiled out below its architecture, in both trees.
- **The K80 falls back to slower code on two common operations:**
  - `__dp4a` becomes four scalar byte multiplies below sm_61 (`common.cuh:561`). That is quantized matmul, which every Q4/Q8 model uses.
  - Half arithmetic runs as FP32 below sm_60.
- **Upstream adds no new sm_37–sm_86 functions from the table.** Its only new uses are `__nanosleep` for multi-GPU all-reduce and WMMA in a lightning indexer. It also replaced Volta's WMMA flash-attention kernel with `mma m8n8k4`.
- **On these cards, CUDA 11.4 itself costs three things:**
  - `movmatrix` is replaced by a shuffle emulation (`mma.cuh:22`). ollama37 also turns off the MMA flash-attention kernel below CUDA 11.8 (`fattn-mma-f16.cuh:11`); its comment says the emulation gives wrong results, which I didn't check.
  - The CUB library path is not compiled in.
  - Native half max/min is replaced by a float fallback.

  Upstream's other version-gated features (FP8, FP4, PDL) target Hopper and Blackwell.

Both files are untracked, and I made no code changes.

content.thinking: The unpatched build matches the published binary exactly (182 instructions for q4_0), but since whole-kernel totals are skewed by different loop unrolling in the `vmad` build, I'll measure cost per iteration of the hot loop instead.

input.command:
S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-jack-src-ollama37/02c7d8e5-88e9-4d15-a73b-8e1b6ef9c27c/scratchpad/cuda114; cd $S/exp; cat > loops.py <<'EOF'
import re,collections,subprocess,sys
T={'FFMA':192,'FADD':192,'FMUL':192,'IADD':160,'IADD32I':160,'ISUB':160,'LOP':160,'LOP32I':160,'ISETP':160,'ICMP':160,'IMNMX':160,'SEL':160,
   'IMAD':32,'IMUL':32,'IMUL32I':32,'ISCADD':160,'SHR':64,'SHL':64,'SHF':64,'BFE':32,'BFI':32,'I2I':128,'I2F':32,'F2I':32,'F2F':32,'VMAD':32,'PRMT':32,'SHFL':32,'MUFU':32}
def load(p):
    F={};cur=None
    for line in open(p):
        m=re.match(r'\s+Function : (\S+)',line)
        if m: cur=m.group(1); F[cur]=[]; continue
        m=re.search(r'/\*([0-9a-f]{4})\*/\s+(@!?P\d\s+)?([A-Z0-9_.]+)([^;]*);',line)
        if cur and m: F[cur].append((int(m.group(1),16),m.group(3),m.group(4)))
    return F
def hot(ins):
    best=None
    for addr,op,args in ins:
        if op.startswith('BRA'):
            t=re.search(r'0x([0-9a-f]+)',args)
            if t and int(t.group(1),16)<addr:
                body=[o.split('.')[0] for a,o,_ in ins if int(t.group(1),16)<=a<=addr]
                if best is None or len(body)>len(best): best=body
    return best or []
def cost(ops): return sum(1/T[o] for o in ops if o in T)*32
A=load(sys.argv[1]); B=load(sys.argv[2])
names=list(A); D=dict(zip(names,subprocess.run(['c++filt'],input='\n'.join(names),capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split('\n')))
tn={2:'q4_0',3:'q4_1',6:'q5_0',7:'q5_1',8:'q8_0',10:'q2_K',11:'q3_K',12:'q4_K',13:'q5_K',14:'q6_K',20:'iq4_nl',23:'iq4_xs'}
print(f"{'type':7}{'loop a':>7}{'loop b':>7}{'cost a':>8}{'cost b':>8}{'speed-up':>9}  a: mul/extract ops   b: VMAD")
for f in names:
    m=re.match(r'void mul_mat_vec_q<\(ggml_type\)(\d+), 1>',D[f])
    if not m or int(m.group(1)) not in tn: continue
    a,b=hot(A[f]),hot(B[f]); ca,cb=cost(a),cost(b)
    # normalise by multiplies: bytes processed per iteration = VMAD count in b; in a = IMAD+IMUL doing byte products (approx)
    na=sum(a.count(x) for x in ('IMAD','IMUL')); nb=b.count('VMAD')
    print(f"{tn[int(m.group(1))]:7}{len(a):7}{len(b):7}{ca:8.1f}{cb:8.1f}{(ca/max(na,1))/(cb/max(nb,1)) if nb else 0:9.2f}  {collections.Counter(a).most_common(6)}  |  {collections.Counter(b).most_common(6)}")
EOF

# What the K80 runs, and what it could run instead

This study checks the sm_37 code in the published image (`dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`, `10eb85c9`) against everything CUDA 11.4 offers sm_37. It then tests one rewrite. Nothing ran on a GPU.

**Method**
- **Real K80 code:** `cuobjdump -sass -arch sm_37` on the image's `libggml-cuda.so`. 122 cubins, 3,554 sm_37 kernels.
- **Rewrite test:** the CUDA 11.4 `nvcc` (11.4.152) compiled the real `mmvq.cu` for sm_37 twice, as-is and with the patch in §3 applied to a scratch copy. It ran inside a `gcc:10` container, CPU only. The unpatched build reproduces the image exactly: q4_0 decode is 182 instructions in both.
- **Cost model:** instructions weighted by the cc 3.5/3.7 column of the CUDA 11.4 Programming Guide throughput table ("Throughput of Native Arithmetic Instructions").

## 1. Kepler throughput that matters (results per clock per SM, cc 3.7)

| Instruction | Throughput | Instruction | Throughput |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| FP32 add/mul/FMA | 192 | 32-bit integer multiply, multiply-add (`IMAD`) | **32** |
| 32-bit integer add, AND/OR/XOR, compare | 160 | Bit-field extract/insert (`BFE`) | **32** |
| SIMD video `vabsdiff4` | 160 | All other video instructions (`VMAD` …) | 32 |
| 8/16-bit → 32-bit int conversion (`I2I`) | 128 | int↔float and other conversions (`I2F`, `F2F`) | 32 |
| 32-bit shift | 64 | Warp shuffle | 32 |

On the K80 an integer multiply costs six FP32 FMAs, and so does a bit-field extract.

## 2. Does the K80 get every basic function it should?

CUDA 11.4 declares **287** functions usable on sm_37: `crt/device_functions.h` and `sm_20/30/32/35_intrinsics.h`. ollama37's ggml-cuda calls 16 of them by name. The rest fall into these groups:

| Group | Functions | Status on the K80 |
|---|---|---|
| **Used by name** | `__shfl_xor_sync` (25), `__vsub4` (20), `__vsubss4` (14), `__vcmpne4` (12), `__byte_perm` (9), `__shfl_sync`, `__shfl_up_sync`, `__all_sync`, `__any_sync`, `__syncwarp`, `__syncthreads(_or)`, `__umulhi`, `__hadd`, `__ldg`, `__trap` | ✓ |
| **Not called by name, but the compiler emits it anyway** | `__ldg` → the decode kernels load through `LDG.E.T`, the read-only cache, because the pointers are `const __restrict__`. `__expf`/`__logf`/`__fdividef` → `-use_fast_math` is on (`ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt:129`), giving 21k `MUFU` instructions. Byte extracts → `BFE`/`PRMT`. | ✓ Nothing to gain by naming them |
| **Not relevant to inference** | Directed-rounding float/double math (`__fadd_rd` …), double conversions, `__brev`, `__clz`, `__popc`, `__ffs`, `__sad`, profiling | — |
| **Unused SIMD video** | `__vadd4`, `__vmaxs4`, `__vabsdiffs4`, `__vsads4` … | No dot-product use. `vabsdiff4` is fast (160) but computes \|a−b\|, not a·b. |
| **Missing: PTX only, not in the header table** | Scalar video `vmad` with byte select (PTX, sm_20+) | ✗ **Not used — see §3** |

Also checked in the real decode kernels (`mul_mat_vec_q<type, 1>`):
- **No register spills:** `LOCAL:0`, and no `STL`/`LDL` in the ncols=1 kernels.
- **Every weight load uses `LDG.E.T`.**

So the memory side already uses what Kepler has. The waste is in the arithmetic.

## 3. The rewrite: `ggml_cuda_dp4a` fallback → `vmad`

**Why it matters for the K80:**
- MMQ is disabled below cc 610 (`mmq.cu:444`), so prompt processing on the K80 goes to cuBLAS.
- Every generated token of a quantized model goes through MMVQ → `vecdotq.cuh`, which calls `ggml_cuda_dp4a` at 56 sites.
- On sm_37 `ggml_cuda_dp4a` falls back to scalar C (`common.cuh:563-565`). Per byte, that compiles to one `BFE`/`PRMT` sign extract, one nibble extract and one `IMAD`: two or three instructions at 32/clk.

**The replacement:**

```cuda
asm("vmad.s32.s32.s32 %0, %1.b0, %2.b0, %0;\n\t"
    "vmad.s32.s32.s32 %0, %1.b1, %2.b1, %0;\n\t"
    "vmad.s32.s32.s32 %0, %1.b2, %2.b2, %0;\n\t"
    "vmad.s32.s32.s32 %0, %1.b3, %2.b3, %0;" : "+r"(c) : "r"(a), "r"(b));
```

Each `vmad` selects one byte from each operand, sign-extends both, multiplies, and adds. That is the same signed×signed arithmetic as `__dp4a`. `ptxas` 11.4 turns each one into a single native `VMAD` on sm_37.

**Micro-test, 8 dp4a calls, sm_37 SASS:**

| Variant | ALU instructions | Mix | Weighted slots |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| Current fallback | 128 | 34 `IMAD`, 48 `BFE`, 16 `PRMT` … | 105 |
| `vmad` | 64 | 32 `VMAD`, 3 `IMAD` … | 41 |
| `cvt.s32.s8` (`I2I`, 128/clk) | 160 | the compiler turned it back into `BFE` + `PRMT` | 137 ✗ |

**Real `mmvq.cu`, decode hot loop, cost per weight load** (weighted slots ÷ `LDG` in the loop; the `vmad` build unrolls some loops 2×, so per-load is the fair unit):

| Type | Current | `vmad` | Fewer ALU slots |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| q4_0 | 5.9 | 3.6 | 1.66× |
| q8_0 | 4.8 | 3.0 | 1.59× |
| q6_K | 4.6 | 3.0 | 1.53× |
| q3_K | 5.1 | 3.6 | 1.43× |
| q4_K | 6.8 | 5.7 | 1.21× |
| iq4_xs | 10.0 | 6.0 | 1.67× |

The derivation (slots and `LDG` counts per loop):
- q4_0: 59.3/10 → 71.6/20
- q8_0: 76.1/16 → 95.9/32
- q6_K: 50.8/11 → 66.2/22
- q3_K: 106.9/21 → 74.9/21
- q4_K: 82.1/12 → 68.1/12
- iq4_xs: 160.1/16 → 96.1/16

**Scope of the patch:**
- **Only one function changes.** It sits in the `#else` branch that sm_61 and newer never compile, so their code is byte-identical.
- **Maxwell and GP100 also get native `VMAD`:** `ptxas` emits `VMAD` for sm_50 and sm_60 too, 26 `VMAD` against 28 `XMAD` + 48 `BFE` in the micro-test. Their `VMAD` throughput is unknown, so the patch could start as `__CUDA_ARCH__ < 500` (Kepler only).

## 4. What this does not prove

- **Speed on the K80 is not measured.** Fewer ALU slots only helps as far as decode is ALU-bound. The K80's low bandwidth use (about 53 of 240 GB/s from earlier CI numbers) suggests it is, but the real gain has to be measured.
- **`VMAD` throughput on sm_37 is assumed to be 32.** That comes from the guide's "all other SIMD video instructions" row. `PRMT` is not in the table and was costed at 32.
- **Correctness is not tested on hardware.** The semantics come from the PTX ISA definition of `vmad`.

## 5. Next steps, in order

1. **Correctness:** run `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` on a K80 with the patch, against the CPU backend.
2. **Speed:** run `ollama37-ci-perf` decode tok/s on the K80, patched vs unpatched, at short and long context, on q4_0, q4_K_M and q8_0 models.
3. **Scope:** keep the patch only if both pass. Decide whether to extend it to sm_50/52/60 after a Maxwell or P100 measurement.

- **`VMAD` throughput on sm_37 is assumed to be 32.** That comes from the guide's "all other SIMD video instructions" row. `PRMT` is not in the table and was costed at 32.
- **Correctness is not tested on hardware.** The semantics come from the PTX ISA definition of `vmad`.

1. **Correctness:** run `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` on a K80 with the patch, against the CPU backend.
2. **Speed:** run `ollama37-ci-perf` decode tok/s on the K80, patched vs unpatched, at short and long context, on q4_0, q4_K_M and q8_0 models.
3. **Scope:** keep the patch only if both pass. Decide whether to extend it to sm_50/52/60 after a Maxwell or P100 measurement.

content.text:
The K80 does use the basic functions well: its memory loads already take the fast path. The weak spot is the integer math in the fallback for `__dp4a` (a 4-byte dot product, sm_61 and newer). I found a rewrite from CUDA 11.4 that cuts that math by 1.2–1.7× in the loop that runs for every generated token. Nothing ran on a GPU, so the real tok/s gain is unmeasured. The study is in `cuda-11.4-sm37-study.md`.

**How I checked:** I read the real K80 machine code out of the published image `10eb85c9`, where the CUDA library has 3,554 sm_37 kernels. I compiled the real `mmvq.cu` with the CUDA 11.4 compiler for sm_37. My unpatched build matches the image exactly, so the comparison is fair. I weighted each instruction by Kepler's throughput from NVIDIA's CUDA 11.4 guide.

**Does the K80 get every basic function?** For memory and math library calls, yes:
- **Available vs used:** CUDA 11.4 offers 287 functions on sm_37, and ollama37 calls 16 of them by name.
- **Memory side:** the compiler already routes every weight load through the read-only cache (`LDG.E.T`), and the decode kernels don't spill registers.
- **Fast math:** `-use_fast_math` already turns `expf`, `logf` and division into the fast versions.
- **What's left:** the unused functions are either irrelevant to inference or can't compute a dot product.

**Where the K80 loses time:**
- The K80 can't use MMQ, so every generated token of a quantized model goes through MMVQ. That calls the `ggml_cuda_dp4a` fallback at 56 sites.
- On sm_37 each byte costs an integer multiply-add plus one or two bit-field extracts. Kepler runs each of those at 32 per clock, against 192 for FP32 math.

**The rewrite:** replace the fallback with four `vmad` instructions. `vmad` is a PTX multiply-add that picks one byte from each operand, and CUDA 11.4 compiles it to a single native `VMAD` per byte on sm_37.

| Quant type | ALU cost per weight load (current → `vmad`) | Fewer ALU slots |
|---|---|--:|
| q4_0 | 5.9 → 3.6 | 1.66× |
| q8_0 | 4.8 → 3.0 | 1.59× |
| q6_K | 4.6 → 3.0 | 1.53× |
| q3_K | 5.1 → 3.6 | 1.43× |
| q4_K | 6.8 → 5.7 | 1.21× |
| iq4_xs | 10.0 → 6.0 | 1.67× |

- **Cards on sm_61 and newer are unaffected.** The patch changes one function, in a branch they never compile.
- **One idea failed:** sign-extending bytes through the faster conversion instruction (`cvt.s32.s8`) came out worse, because the compiler turned it back into extracts.

**What is still unproven:**
- **Speed:** whether fewer ALU slots means more tok/s on a K80. It only helps as far as decode is limited by arithmetic rather than memory.
- **Assumed costs:** I assumed `VMAD` runs at 32 per clock and costed `PRMT` at 32, because neither appears by name in NVIDIA's table.
- **Correctness:** the patch has not been run on hardware. It relies on the PTX definition of `vmad` (signed×signed, like `__dp4a`).

**Next steps:**
1. Check correctness: run `test-backend-ops -o MUL_MAT` on a K80.
2. Measure speed: run `ollama37-ci-perf` on q4_0, q4_K_M and q8_0 models, with and without the patch.

The repo is unchanged apart from the three untracked `cuda-11.4-*.md` files; the patch exists only in a scratch copy. The `gcc:10` image I pulled to run the compiler is still on the host, and you can remove it with `docker rmi gcc:10`. If you want, I can file an issue for the `vmad` patch with this evidence and the two hardware checks.

content: You wanted to know whether the K80 makes the best use of CUDA 11.4; the study found a vmad rewrite that cuts decode integer math 1.2–1.7×. Next, check that patch on a real K80 for correctness and tok/s.

| Type | Current | `vmad` | Fewer slots |

| iq4_xs | 10.01 | 6.01 | 1.67× |
| q8_0 | 4.75 | 3.00 | 1.59× |
| q6_K | 4.62 | 3.01 | 1.53× |
| q3_K | 5.09 | 3.57 | 1.43× |
| q4_K | 6.84 | 5.67 | 1.21× |

- [ ] A decision on sm_50/52/60 is recorded: Kepler-only, or extended after a measurement.

content.content:
=== ollama37-ci-build
---
description: >-
  An agent builds the ollama37 image by its own ideas. The agent runs make on
  a dev box. The local build defaults OLLAMA_VERSION to 0.0.0, and the ollama
  registry rejects every gated model pull from it with 412. The image looks
  fine and cannot pull modern models. This skill asks the agent to build the
  image by the steps below, not by its own ideas.
---

Build the ollama37 image with CI:
1. Check the version the build injects with `gh variable list` (`OLLAMA_VERSION`).
2. Run the full build suite with `gh workflow run test-build.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37`, with no `test_id`, so `TC-BUILD-004` retags `ollama37:latest` to `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`.
3. Wait for it with `gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status`.
4. Confirm the retag with `gh run view <run-id> --log | grep 'retagged sha256'`.
5. Apply the image with the `ollama37-ci-apply` skill.
=== ollama37-ci-apply
---
description: >-
  An agent applies a freshly built ollama37 image by its own ideas. The agent
  runs docker compose on the host by hand. The hand recreate leaves no log,
  and after a build that skipped the retag it recreates the previous image.
  Every test after it silently exercises stale code. This skill asks the agent
  to apply the image by the steps below, not by its own ideas.
---

Apply the ollama37 image with CI:
1. Confirm the build run retagged the image: `gh run view <build-run> --log | grep 'retagged sha256'`.
2. Stop when the grep finds nothing, and rerun the retag with `gh workflow run test-build.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37 -f test_id=TC-BUILD-004`.
3. Run `gh workflow run test-runtime.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37`; it recreates the container from `dogkeeper886/ollama37:latest`, and host B's `sm61` / `sm86` run the models suite only.
4. Wait for it with `gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status`.
5. Test the applied image with the suite workflows (`test-inference.yml`, `test-models.yml`) on the same `runner_label`.
=== ollama37-ci-perf
---
description: >-
  An agent measures a CUDA or flash-attention change by its own ideas. The
  agent times a hand curl loop on a one-line prompt. The single run never
  checks the answer, and a short prompt once hid a 7.4x flash-attention
  regression on the K80 behind a 22% one. The number cannot decide whether to
  keep the change. This skill asks the agent to measure the change by the
  steps below, not by its own ideas.
---

Run an ollama37 performance experiment with CI:
1. Build each path's kernel routing on its own branch with the `ollama37-ci-build` skill.
2. Run each path with `gh workflow run test-throughput.yml --ref <branch> -f runner_label=sm37 -f models=<model> -f flash_attention=<0|1> -f kv_cache_type='' -f context_size=8192 -f num_predict=128 -f judge_mode=dual`.
3. Wait for it with `gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status`.
4. Confirm the run summary shows the agent judge's verdict, not a fallback to the simple judge.
5. Record Prompt tok/s, Gen tok/s and Check for each path from the run summary.
6. Record a crashed path as unusable; the workflow reverts the testbed to `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=0` itself.
7. Compare the paths on the same model and context.

id: TC-MODELS-008
name: gemma3:270m Inference
suite: models
priority: 4
timeout: 600000
dependencies: []
issue: 55
intent:
  user_story: |
    Verify gemma3:270m answers on the K80

steps:
  - name: Test inference
    command: |
      out=$(curl -s $OLLAMA_HOST/api/generate \
        -d '{"model":"gemma3:270m","prompt":"What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence.","stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":400,"temperature":0,"seed":0}}')
      echo "$out" | jq -r '"response: " + (.response // "" | .[0:400])'
      echo "$out" | jq -c '{error, done, done_reason, eval_count}'
      # A reply with nothing to read, or one short unit over and over, is broken whatever it
      # says. Flag it here: the simple judge fails it, and the agent judge never reads it.
      echo "$out" | jq -r 'select(.error == null) | (.response // "" | sub("\\s+$"; "")) as $r | ($r | length) as $n
        | if ($r | test("[\\p{L}\\p{N}]") | not) then "REPLY_NO_TEXT"
          elif any(range(1; 51); . as $u | $n >= ([100, 5 * $u] | max) and (($r[0:$u] * (($n / $u | ceil) + 1))[0:$n] == $r)) then "REPLY_REPEAT"
          else empty end' 2>/dev/null
      { [ -n "$out" ] && echo "$out" | jq -e '.error == null and .done == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; } \
        && echo "LOAD_OK" || echo "LOAD_FAIL"
    expectPatterns:
      - "LOAD_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "LOAD_FAIL"
      - "REPLY_NO_TEXT"
      - "REPLY_REPEAT"
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"

  - name: Check GPU memory
    command: docker exec $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
    expectPatterns:
      - "[0-9]+ MiB"

  - name: Check GPU count
    command: |
      # Die placement is not deterministic across loads: now and then a model spills a
      # small allocation onto one die more than it needs. Reload once before calling
      # it a regression; overshooting twice is one.
      die_check() {
        pids=$(docker top $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER -eo pid | tail -n +2 | paste -sd'|')
        output=$(docker exec $OLLAMA37_CONTAINER nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=gpu_uuid,pid,used_memory --format=csv,noheader \
          | awk -F', ' -v p="^($pids)$" '$2 ~ p')
        echo "$output"
        active=$(echo "$output" | cut -d, -f1 | sort -u | grep -c .)
        total=$(echo "$output" | grep -oP '[0-9]+(?= MiB)' | paste -sd+ | bc)
        echo "Active GPUs: $active, Total VRAM: ${total} MiB"
        [ "$active" -le 1 ] || [ "$total" -gt $(( (active - 1) * 11441 )) ]
      }
      if die_check; then
        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      else
        echo "RELOAD: ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs but using $active; reloading once"
        curl -s $OLLAMA_HOST/api/generate -d '{"model":"gemma3:270m","keep_alive":0}' >/dev/null

**Finding: why the port is taken.** The K80 runner sets `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`. Your pipeline's Models job stopped that unit at the end and restarted the yielded service, which now holds 11434. #513 taught `test-models.yml` to yield the GPU this way; `test-throughput.yml`, and `test-runtime.yml` via compose, don't. So the same bind error would also hit the `ollama37-ci-apply` path while that service runs.

**Finding: a baseline exists anyway.** Your pipeline's Models artifacts measured the unpatched image (`e4295e8e`) on the K80 with every model fully on the GPU:
- **TC-MODELS-008**, gemma3:270m Q8_0: 119.6 tok/s decode
- **TC-MODELS-003**, deepseek-r1:1.5b Q4_K: 35.68 tok/s decode
- **TC-MODELS-023**, llama3.1:8b Q4_K: 12.48 tok/s decode

**Done so far:**
- **Patch:** committed as `109aaa79` on `fix-522-vmad-dp4a` and pushed. No PR is open.
- **Criterion 3:** the `mmvq.cu` machine code is byte-identical on sm_50 through sm_86. Only sm_37 changes, and it gains 34,224 `VMAD`.
- **Leftover on the K80 host:** my failed run left a stopped `ollama37` container in the `Created` state, plus a `docker_default` network, in the runner workspace. The next compose run replaces them.

**Recommend, since the next step is your choice:**
- **Option 1 (recommended):** measure through `test-models.yml`, which already yields the GPU. Build the branch with `test-build.yml` on sm37 (its `TC-BUILD-004` retags `:latest`). Then run `test-models.yml` for `TC-MODELS-008`, `003` and `023`. The unit restarts on the patched `:latest`, and I compare decode tok/s and the greedy responses against the baseline above. This skips `test-runtime`, which departs from the `ollama37-ci-apply` skill, and it uses short prompts, not the skill's 8192-context throughput run.
- **Option 2:** stop the yielded service on the K80 host yourself for the experiment. The standard `ollama37-ci-perf` path (`test-runtime` + `test-throughput`) then works as written.
- **Option 3:** fix `test-throughput.yml` to yield like `test-models.yml` first, as a separate issue.

**Next step:** tell me 1, 2 or 3. With 1, I start the branch build on sm37 right away.

The second run failed the same way as the first: `bind: address already in use` on port 11434, in "Apply experiment environment" (run 36323704693). So something on the K80 host still holds the port. I can't see the host from here. These commands, run on the K80 host, will show what holds it:

```bash
# Which process owns 11434
sudo ss -ltnp 'sport = :11434'

# Any container publishing it, and which compose project or unit started it
docker ps -a --filter publish=11434 --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Label "com.docker.compose.project"}}'

# The ollama37 user units and the runner's service settings
systemctl --user list-units 'ollama37-*' --all
grep -E 'OLLAMA37_(SERVICE|YIELD_SERVICE|CONTAINER)|OLLAMA_HOST' ~/actions-runner/.env
```

- **Likely culprit:** the unit named in `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE`, or a container from another compose project. Stopping that one lets `test-throughput` bind the port.
- **Not the cause:** the stopped `ollama37` containers my failed runs left behind. They are `Created`, never started, so they don't hold the port.

If you'd rather not change the host again, option 1 still works: measure through `test-models.yml`, which does its own yield and restore. Paste the output and I'll take it from there.

54	jobs:
    55	  models:
    56	    name: Models Tests
    57	    runs-on: [self-hosted, "${{ inputs.runner_label || 'sm37' }}"]
    58	    environment: cicd-1
    59	    env:
    60	      OLLAMA37_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}
    61	      OLLAMA_DEBUG: ${{ inputs.debug && '1' || '' }}
    62	    outputs:
    63	      result: ${{ steps.models-tests.outcome }}
    64	
    65	    steps:
    66	      - name: Checkout
    67	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
    68	
    69	      - name: Identify host
    70	        uses: ./.github/actions/identify-host
    71	
    72	      - name: Setup Node.js
    73	        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    74	        with:
    75	          node-version: "20"
    76	
    77	      - name: Install test runner dependencies
    78	        run: cd cicd/tests && npm ci
    79	
    80	      - name: Yield GPU
    81	        run: |
    82	          [ -n "${OLLAMA37_SERVICE:-}" ] || { echo "No OLLAMA37_SERVICE on this host"; exit 0; }
    83	          systemctl --user stop 'ollama37-*'
    84	          if [ -n "${OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE:-}" ]; then systemctl --user stop "$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE"; fi
    85	          systemctl --user start "$OLLAMA37_SERVICE"
    86	          # integer >= 1 tries, 2 s apart
    87	          for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sf "${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://localhost:11434}/api/tags" >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 2; done
    88	          echo "::error::$OLLAMA37_SERVICE did not come up"; exit 1
    89	
    90	      - name: Run models tests
    91	        id: models-tests
    92	        env:
    93	          # simple | dual
    94	          JUDGE_MODE: simple
    95	        run: |
    96	          cd cicd/tests
    97	          echo "Judge mode: ${JUDGE_MODE}"
    98	
    99	          # Build test ID flag if provided
   100	          ID_FLAG=""
   101	          if [ -n "${{ inputs.test_id }}" ]; then
   102	            ID_FLAG="--id ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
   103	            echo "Running single test: ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
   104	          fi
   105	
   106	          # Run models tests. No gpu-temp-guard: its 80°C abort killed full-suite runs
   107	          # (35549667518, peak 81°C at case 9 of 19) while the K80 itself only slows at
   108	          # 88°C and shuts down at 93°C. The card's own thresholds are the protection
   109	          # here. A non-zero exit stays tolerated — the JSON below is the gate.
   110	          # --output-dir: any path, same in the Agent judge step
   111	          npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models $ID_FLAG --output-dir ../results/models --format json > /tmp/models-results.json || true
   112	
   113	          echo "--- JSON Results ---"
   114	          cat /tmp/models-results.json
   115	
   116	      - name: Unload test models from VRAM
   117	        if: always()
   118	        run: |
   119	          echo "Unloading test models from VRAM..."
   120	          # Derived from the suite, so adding or removing a testcase needs no edit here.
   121	          for m in $(grep -ohE '"model":"[^"]+"' cicd/tests/testcases/models/*.yml | cut -d'"' -f4 | sort -u); do
   122	            curl -s ${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://localhost:11434}/api/generate -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"keep_alive\":0}" || true
   123	          done
   124	          echo "Models unloaded"
   125	
   126	      - name: Restore GPU
   127	        if: always()
   128	        run: |
   129	          [ -n "${OLLAMA37_SERVICE:-}" ] || exit 0
   130	          systemctl --user stop "$OLLAMA37_SERVICE"
   131	          [ -n "${OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE:-}" ] || exit 0
   132	          systemctl --user is-enabled --quiet "$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE" || exit 0
   133	          systemctl --user start "$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE"
   134	          # integer >= 1 tries, 2 s apart
   135	          for i in $(seq 1 60); do curl -sf "${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://localhost:11434}/api/tags" >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 2; done
   136	          echo "::error::$OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE did not come back"; exit 1
   137	
   138	      - name: Agent judge
   139	        if: ${{ !cancelled() && (inputs.judge_mode || 'dual') == 'dual' }}
   140	        env:
   141	          # simple | dual
   142	          JUDGE_MODE: dual
   143	          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
   144	          # JUDGE_BASE_URL (cicd-1 variable) points the judge at an ollama server
   145	          # instead of Anthropic — a judge off the box under test. Unset it and
   146	          # the judge falls back to Claude on the OAuth token above; the auth
   147	          # token has to follow the base URL or it would break that fallback.
   148	          ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL }}
   149	          ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && 'ollama' || '' }}
   150	          ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
   151	          # Claude Code's side-call model; ollama has no haiku tag to serve it.
   152	          ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
   153	        run: |
   154	          cd cicd/tests
   155	          # the Run models tests step's --output-dir
   156	          npx tsx src/cli.ts judge ../results/models --format json > /tmp/models-results.json || true
   157	          cat /tmp/models-results.json
   158	
   159	      - name: Check test results
   160	        run: |
   161	          FAILED=$(jq '.summary.failed' /tmp/models-results.json)
   162	          echo "Failed tests: $FAILED"
   163	          if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
   164	            echo "::error::$FAILED models test(s) failed"
   165	            exit 1
   166	          fi
   167	
   168	      - name: Upload models results
   169	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   170	        if: always()
   171	        with:
   172	          name: models-test-results
   173	          path: |
   174	            /tmp/models-results.json
   175	            cicd/results/

content.text:
Your assumption is **half right**. The workflow needs a rewrite, but the script doesn't.

**The workflow does need a rewrite.** `.github/workflows/test-throughput.yml` never touches `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` and assumes compose owns the testbed:

| Step | test-throughput.yml | test-models.yml |
|---|---|---|
| Before tests | `cd docker && docker compose up -d --force-recreate` with `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION`/`OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE` (`:99-109`) | **Yield GPU:** stop `ollama37-*` and `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE`, start `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, wait for `/api/tags` (`:80-88`) |
| After tests | `always()` → `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` again with FA=0 (`:153-160`) | **Restore GPU:** stop `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, restart the yield service if it is enabled (`:126-136`) |
| `OLLAMA37_ROOT` | not set | `github.workspace` (`:60`) |

On the K80 host a service holds 11434, so both compose steps fail with `bind: address already in use`. That is what failed runs 36314898422 and 36323704693.

**The script doesn't need a rewrite.** `bench-throughput` (`cli.ts:307`, `perf/throughput.ts`, `perf/capture.ts`) is already service-agnostic:
- It talks only to `OLLAMA_HOST` over HTTP.
- It pulls a missing model itself (`ensureModel`, `throughput.ts:62-69`). I told you earlier that throughput doesn't pull models; that was wrong.
- It unloads each model when it's done.

It never runs `docker` or `compose`, so it works against whatever server the workflow brings up.

**Two more workflows use the same compose pattern:** `test-context.yml` and `test-mlx-smoke.yml`. Only `test-models.yml` handles the service.

**Open design question for the rewrite:** FA and KV-cache type are experiment knobs. Today they reach the server as compose env vars. Under the service model, the workflow needs another way to pass them to `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, for example a per-run unit drop-in or `systemctl --user set-environment`, and to undo it in the restore step. That depends on how the K80 host's unit is defined, which I can't see from here.

I haven't changed anything. If you want, I can file this as an issue covering all three workflows.

input.content:
Since #513, a host that shares its GPUs names its server under test as a user systemd unit (`OLLAMA37_SERVICE`). `test-models.yml` yields the GPU to that unit before its tests and restores it afterwards. `test-throughput.yml` was never updated. It still applies the experiment environment by force-recreating the compose container from its own checkout, and its `always()` revert recreates it again. On the K80 host the yielded service holds port 11434, so both steps fail with `bind: address already in use`, and no throughput run can measure anything there. This blocks the #522 perf comparison (runs 36314898422 and 36323704693). The fix is to rewrite the workflow's setup and revert steps to yield and restore the GPU the way `test-models.yml` does, and to carry the flash-attention and KV-cache knobs to the service. Session log: [`.sessions/02c7d8e5-88e9-4d15-a73b-8e1b6ef9c27c.jsonl`](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/blob/main/.sessions/02c7d8e5-88e9-4d15-a73b-8e1b6ef9c27c.jsonl).

## Where the two workflows differ

| Step | `test-throughput.yml` | `test-models.yml` |
|---|---|---|
| Before tests | `cd docker && docker compose up -d --force-recreate` with `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION` / `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE` (`:99-109`) | **Yield GPU:** stop `ollama37-*` and `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE`, start `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, wait for `/api/tags` (`:80-88`) |
| After tests | `always()`: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` with FA=0 (`:153-160`) | **Restore GPU:** stop `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, restart the yield service if it is enabled (`:126-136`) |
| `OLLAMA37_ROOT` | not set | `${{ github.workspace }}` (`:60`) |

Both failed runs stop in "Apply experiment environment":

```
Error starting userland proxy: listen tcp4 0.0.0.0:11434: bind: address already in use
```

The "Revert to stable baseline" step then fails the same way. Each failed run also leaves a `Created` (never started) `ollama37` container and a `docker_default` network in the runner workspace.

## What already works

- **`bench-throughput` needs no change** (`cicd/tests/src/cli.ts:307`, `perf/throughput.ts`, `perf/capture.ts`).
- **It talks only to `OLLAMA_HOST` over HTTP.**
- **It pulls a missing model itself** (`ensureModel`, `throughput.ts:62-69`).
- **It unloads each model when it's done.**
- **It never calls `docker` or `compose`.**

## Open question

The workflow's `flash_attention` and `kv_cache_type` inputs reach the server today as compose environment variables. Under a service, the rewrite needs another route to `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, for example a per-run unit drop-in or `systemctl --user set-environment`. The restore step must undo it, and the route depends on how each host defines its unit.

## Out of scope

`test-context.yml` and `test-mlx-smoke.yml` share the compose pattern. They need the same treatment in their own issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Setup and restore:** `test-throughput.yml` yields the GPU to `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` before the benchmark and restores the yield service after it, in an `always()` step, on a host that sets `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`.
- [ ] **Other hosts:** on a host without `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, the workflow keeps working as today.
- [ ] **Knobs:** `flash_attention` and `kv_cache_type` still reach the server under test, and the restore step leaves the service with its own settings.
- [ ] **Proof:** a `test-throughput.yml` run on `sm37` with `flash_attention=0` passes and reports Prompt tok/s, Gen tok/s and Check for each model.

It still applies the experiment environment by force-recreating the compose container from its own checkout, and its `always()` revert recreates it again. On the K80 host the yielded service holds port 11434, so both steps fail with `bind: address already in use`, and no throughput run can measure anything there. This blocks the #522 perf comparison (runs 36314898422 and 36323704693). The fix is to rewrite the workflow's setup and revert steps to yield and restore the GPU the way `test-models.yml` does, and to carry the flash-attention and KV-cache knobs to the service. Session log: [`.sessions/02c7d8e5-88e9-4d15-a73b-8e1b6ef9c27c.jsonl`](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/blob/main/.sessions/02c7d8e5-88e9-4d15-a73b-8e1b6ef9c27c.jsonl).

## Where the two workflows differ

| Step | `test-throughput.yml` | `test-models.yml` |
|---|---|---|
| Before tests | `cd docker && docker compose up -d --force-recreate` with `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION` / `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE` (`:99-109`) | **Yield GPU:** stop `ollama37-*` and `OLLAMA37_YIELD_SERVICE`, start `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, wait for `/api/tags` (`:80-88`) |
| After tests | `always()`: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` with FA=0 (`:153-160`) | **Restore GPU:** stop `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, restart the yield service if it is enabled (`:126-136`) |
| `OLLAMA37_ROOT` | not set | `${{ github.workspace }}` (`:60`) |

Both failed runs stop in "Apply experiment environment":

```
Error starting userland proxy: listen tcp4 0.0.0.0:11434: bind: address already in use
```

The "Revert to stable baseline" step then fails the same way. Each failed run also leaves a `Created` (never started) `ollama37` container and a `docker_default` network in the runner workspace.

## What already works

- **`bench-throughput` needs no change** (`cicd/tests/src/cli.ts:307`, `perf/throughput.ts`, `perf/capture.ts`).
- **It talks only to `OLLAMA_HOST` over HTTP.**
- **It pulls a missing model itself** (`ensureModel`, `throughput.ts:62-69`).
- **It unloads each model when it's done.**
- **It never calls `docker` or `compose`.**

## Open question

The workflow's `flash_attention` and `kv_cache_type` inputs reach the server today as compose environment variables. Under a service, the rewrite needs another route to `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, for example a per-run unit drop-in or `systemctl --user set-environment`. The restore step must undo it, and the route depends on how each host defines its unit.

## Out of scope

`test-context.yml` and `test-mlx-smoke.yml` share the compose pattern. They need the same treatment in their own issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Setup and restore:** `test-throughput.yml` yields the GPU to `OLLAMA37_SERVICE` before the benchmark and restores the yield service after it, in an `always()` step, on a host that sets `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`.
- [ ] **Other hosts:** on a host without `OLLAMA37_SERVICE`, the workflow keeps working as today.
- [ ] **Knobs:** `flash_attention` and `kv_cache_type` still reach the server under test, and the restore step leaves the service with its own settings.
- [ ] **Proof:** a `test-throughput.yml` run on `sm37` with `flash_attention=0` passes and reports Prompt tok/s, Gen tok/s and Check for each model.
